text: In a forest deep where shadows creep, I pace alone, afraid. day to leap. My roar was loud. My man was fine. But fear made cowards of beasts like mine. I dreamed of courage, bold and bright, but trembled at the smallest fright. A rustle run, a breeze I'd hide. Though jungle kings should stand with pride.

Then came a girl with storm wash shoes. A tin man dented by old blues. A straw stuffed man who sought his brain and welcome me. Despite my shame through poppy fields and haunted wood, I followed where the brave one stood. Each step a quake, each choice a test. Yet still I march, though not the best. In arms I kn before the flame and found a metal. Not just fame, but proof I'd face my deepest scare and chose to stay, though I could tear. Now thrones may gleam and trumpets cheer, but courage is the act of near. The trembling breath, the shaky paw that walks through fear

And stands in  awe. Heat. Heat.  I may not roar with thunder's might, but still I roar and still I fight. For I have learned through doubt and in that cowardice is where I begin and courage is what I carry
